questions.question: What is the operating system's main role between users and hardware?
options: Act as an intermediary and manage hardware use
questions.correctAnswer: Act as an intermediary and manage hardware use
questions.explanation: The OS provides a usable environment while managing hardware and hiding unnecessary hardware complexity.

questions.question: Which list contains the four components of a computer system in the lecture?
questions.explanation: The lecture separates physical resources, their coordinator, application programs, and users.

questions.question: From the system view, why is the OS a resource allocator?
options: It resolves competing requests for efficient and fair resource use
It gives every process unlimited memory
It ensures only one user ever logs in
questions.correctAnswer: It resolves competing requests for efficient and fair resource use
questions.explanation: CPU time, memory, storage, and I/O devices are finite resources the OS must allocate.

questions.question: What is the kernel in the lecture's definition?
options: The program running at all times and forming the OS core
Every application supplied by a vendor
questions.correctAnswer: The program running at all times and forming the OS core
questions.explanation: The kernel is part of the operating system; system programs and applications are separate categories.

questions.question: Which component is hardware that manages a particular kind of I/O device?
questions.explanation: A controller is hardware with registers and a local buffer; a driver is OS software that manages it.

questions.question: What does a device driver provide to the rest of the operating system?
options: A uniform interface to a device controller
questions.correctAnswer: A uniform interface to a device controller
questions.explanation: The driver understands the controller and hides device-specific details behind a uniform interface.

questions.question: How can a controller notify the CPU that an I/O operation has finished?
questions.explanation: An interrupt signals completion or another event needing CPU attention.

questions.question: What does the interrupt vector contain?
questions.explanation: The vector is a table of pointers used to select the handler for an interrupt.

questions.question: Why are CPU registers and the program counter saved during interrupt handling?
options: So interrupted computation can resume correctly
So the interrupted program must restart
So the device becomes an application
questions.correctAnswer: So interrupted computation can resume correctly
questions.explanation: Preserving CPU state allows the handler to return to the interrupted computation.

questions.question: Which description matches main memory in the lecture?
options: Directly accessible by the CPU and typically volatile
Always nonvolatile and slower than all disks
A set of magnetic disk platters
Storage accessible only through a web browser
questions.correctAnswer: Directly accessible by the CPU and typically volatile
questions.explanation: Main memory is typically DRAM and loses its contents without power.

questions.question: What is a key purpose of secondary storage?
options: Replace CPU registers with faster registers
Guarantee faster access than main memory
questions.explanation: Secondary storage retains data and is generally larger but slower than main memory.

questions.question: What is the basic idea of caching?
options: Temporarily copy information from slower storage to faster storage
Always read the slowest storage first
Make every storage level equally large
Convert volatile memory into magnetic disks
questions.correctAnswer: Temporarily copy information from slower storage to faster storage
questions.explanation: The faster cache is checked first; a miss requires obtaining the data from the slower level.

questions.question: After DMA setup, who transfers a block between the device buffer and main memory?
options: The device controller without CPU intervention for each transfer
A text editor for each byte
questions.correctAnswer: The device controller without CPU intervention for each transfer
questions.explanation: DMA allows bulk transfer while the CPU performs other work; completion is signaled per block.

questions.question: Why does multiprogramming switch jobs when one waits for I/O?
options: To keep the CPU useful by running another job
To ensure every program runs to completion without waiting
To prevent more than one job residing in memory
To remove the need for scheduling
questions.correctAnswer: To keep the CPU useful by running another job
questions.explanation: Keeping multiple jobs available reduces CPU idle time when one job waits.

questions.question: What distinguishes time sharing from a basic batch multiprogramming system?
options: It requires every process to finish before the next starts
It keeps all programs outside memory
questions.explanation: Time sharing extends multiprogramming with frequent CPU switches and short response times.

questions.question: What does virtual memory allow in the lecture?
options: Execution of processes not completely in main memory
questions.correctAnswer: Execution of processes not completely in main memory
questions.explanation: Virtual memory permits a process to execute even when not all of it is resident in memory.

questions.question: What is the bootstrap program responsible for?
options: Initialize the system and load the kernel
questions.correctAnswer: Initialize the system and load the kernel
questions.explanation: Firmware bootstrap code initializes system components and starts the OS kernel.

questions.question: In the mode-bit convention shown in these slides, which value represents kernel mode?
questions.explanation: The lecture uses 0 for kernel mode and 1 for user mode; this is the convention of the shown model.

questions.question: Where may privileged instructions execute?
questions.explanation: Dual-mode operation protects the OS by restricting privileged operations to kernel mode.

questions.question: Why does the OS configure a timer before scheduling a process?
options: To regain control if the process runs too long
To guarantee the process never waits for I/O
questions.correctAnswer: To regain control if the process runs too long
questions.explanation: A timer interrupt prevents a process from monopolizing the CPU indefinitely.
